task.title: Release lines, labels and public versions
task.shortdesc: Each release line has one live release. Lines group releases by major version, or by minor version for products released as 0.x minors. Labels such as latest and stable, and public lines, give a public site a version menu.

context.p: A reader is served the live release of their own line, worked out from their organization's version. By default a line is a major version: 2.1 and 2.4 readers both read line 2, whose live release is the newest 2.x build. A product whose customers are each on a specific minor version, such as 0.21, 0.22 and 0.23, needs a line per minor version instead.

strow.stentry: The live 0.22 build, or "No documentation has been published for release 0.22.x yet"

step.cmd: Choose lines by minor version for the repository.

stepxmp.p: Or in a seed file, next to the repository: releaseLines: minor.

info.p: The change applies at once, in one transaction, to what is already live: each live release moves to the line its release belongs to. Nothing that is not live comes back: after switching from major to minor, line 0 becomes the line of its live release (say 0.23), and older minors go live again with their next build (request one with POST /admin/api/repos/:id/builds). Switching back merges lines, keeping the newest build of each. A build finishing during the switch publishes to a line of the new setting. Labels and public lines are cleared, as they named the old lines.

step.cmd: Publish each line from its own branch, for example docs/0.23 with releaseRefs ["main", "docs/*"].
Label lines, for example when a release ships.

stepxmp.codeblock: curl -X PUT "$PUBLIC_URL/admin/api/repos/1/lines/0.23/label" -H "$H" \ -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"label":"latest"}' curl -X PUT "$PUBLIC_URL/admin/api/repos/1/lines/0.21/label" -H "$H" \ -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"label":"stable"}'

info.p: A label is on one line at most: putting it on a line takes it off the other. A line can have several. A line can be labelled before its first build is live, so a release workflow can label it right after pushing the branch. Take a label off with DELETE /admin/api/repos/1/lines/0.23/labels/latest.

step.cmd: On a public site, mark the lines anonymous visitors may read besides the default one.
Check the lines with GET /admin/api/repos/1/lines, or on the admin console's overview, which lists each live line with its labels and whether it is public.

section.title: What anonymous visitors of a public site see

ul.li: At /: the line labelled latest while it is live, otherwise the line of the public entitlements' version (otherwise, without public entitlements, the newest line). This is the default line, and it is always public.

Under /v/line/: each live public line, for example /v/0.21/topics/install.html, filtered for the public products and features on that line. Pages, navigation, search, images under /v/line/_assets/, the theme, the logo and PDFs under /v/line/pdf/ are all that line's public view. A signed-in reader gets the same public view there: their own entitlements apply only at /.

A version menu in the header, when more than one line is public: each line with its labels, such as 0.23 (latest), linking to the same page in that line, or to the line's first page when it has no such page. It is a plain <details> with links, so it works without scripts.
Lines that are not public, or not live, do not exist under /v/: their addresses answer exactly as a page that does not exist, and the menu never lists them.
Canonical addresses. Pages of the default line under /v/ carry a <link rel="canonical"> to the same page at /.

Caching. Each line's public view is cached under its own key, apart from / and from readers' views. The version menu is added to each response after the cache, like the account controls. Every change of lines, labels or public lines drops the caches on every replica.

section.p: The prefix /v/ is reserved for this: a topic whose page id starts with v/line/ for a public line is not reachable at /. Private sites have no /v/ pages and no menu.
